title: The Navigator

editorial:
The Navigator is a 1924 American silent comedy directed by Donald Crisp and Buster Keaton. Keaton plays Rollo, a millionaire who boards a ship he thinks is his way out of a rejected proposal. The ship belongs to the father of Betsy, who has also come aboard, and the two end up stranded at sea together. The Internet Archive record notes it was the most financially successful of Keaton's feature-length films made in-house for Metro or MGM.

Duke's Center for the Study of the Public Domain lists it among the 1924 works that entered the US public domain on January 1, 2020, so the 1924 print is free to reuse. The rights trap is the copy, not the film. The Internet Archive copy carries Portuguese subtitles, and any modern copy may add its own music or other new material. Those additions can be protected even though the 1924 images are not. The story, trademark and restoration layers are not yet researched, so they stay undetermined.
faq: Can I reuse footage from The Navigator in my own video?
Yes for the 1924 images. The print is in the US public domain. Check whether your copy has a modern score or added subtitles, and take only the film itself.
Can I use the music that plays on a copy I found online?
Not automatically. The film is silent, so any music on a modern copy is a separate recording or composition. Use music you have cleared, or music that is itself public domain.
